title: Entrepreneurial Approaches to  Problem Identification in Soci
description: Applications of entrepreneurial processes to problem identification. Includes differences between fixed and growth mindsets, components of entrepreneurial ecosystems, use of qualitative and quantitative data for drawing inferences, design thinking methodologies for clarifying problems worth solving and alternative pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Human Resource Management
description: Acquisition, development, retention, and motivation of human resources in support of both employee and organizational goals.

title: Creativity and Innovation
description: Managing creativity, including selling creative ideas to others, scanning for new opportunities, taking creativity to the marketplace, and creating an organizational culture for innovation.

title: Multinational Business and Comparative Management
description: Context of international business, environment, institutions, and business practices. Cultural awareness, sensitivity, interpersonal, and leadership skills needed in an international context.

title: Fundamentals of Entrepreneurship
description: Process of initiating, expanding, purchasing, and consolidating businesses. Concepts, theories, and techniques of managerial innovation and implementation.

title: Management Internship
description: Internship with business firms, government agencies, or nonprofit organizations. Under joint supervision of intern organization and course instructor. Activities for advancing career readiness, applying principles of managing organizations, enhancing leadership skills, and supporting professional development.

title: Global Business & Diplomacy
description: The impact of international affairs and public policy on business strategy and operations. Political and economic diplomacy.

title: Strategic Management
description: Provides a top management perspective on strategy analysis and development. Develops strategic thinking for creating and sustaining competitive advantage in today’s challenging global business environment.

title: Entrepreneurial Opportunity Recognition and Evaluation
description: Core concepts and key elements of recognizing and evaluating new business opportunity to include customer discovery process, design thinking, industry and market analysis, lean startup methodology, market trends, problem-solution validation, and value proposition design.

title: International Entrepreneurship
description: Launching and managing an international entrepreneurial venture. Search and identification of opportunities in foreign markets, logistics of international business expansion, cross-cultural business communication, and international networking.

title: Business Negotiation
description: Origins and strategies of abstract and theoretical approaches to bargaining and negotiation in business situations faced by managers and leaders.

title: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
description: Corporate social responsibility, stakeholder theory, morality of capitalism, and corporate governance. Ethical theory and its application to ongoing issues and current events within the business context.

title: Family Business Management
description: Managing a family owned business. Succession planning, governance, strategy and family dynamics of mixing family and business roles, non-family employees, and culture.

title: Social Entrepreneurship
description: Entrepreneurial skills to craft innovative responses to social needs. Social mission, launching and building a social venture and developing social returns to an enterprise.

title: Franchise Management
description: Franchising presented as a viable alternative path to entrepreneurship. Nature and role of franchisor and franchisee including challenges of becoming a franchisee of an existing system and of becoming a franchisor.

title: Business Model Design and Development
description: Core concepts and key elements of producing a business plan for a new entrepreneurial opportunity to include designing experiments to validate critical business model assumptions and assess product-market fit.

title: Human Resource Selection
description: Employee selection and placement issues in organizations including strategic, legal, and measurement issues. Roles of recruitment, job analysis, and human resource planning in human resource selection process.

title: Compensation
description: Wage and salary administration in organizations. Determinants of general wage and salary levels and structures. Total compensation systems, interrelationship among employee performance, intrinsic and extrinsic rewards, pay equity, and employee pay satisfaction.

title: Performance Management
description: Definition, measurement, and evaluation of employee performance, development of employee skills, and implementation of a performance management system.

title: Legal Issues in Managing Employees
description: Statutes, case law, and legal issues relevant to managers, including recruitment, hiring, wages and hours, discrimination, sexual harassment, occupational safety and health, firing and post-termination. Focus on California and federal laws that managers need to know.

title: International Human Resource Management
description: Human resource issue facing multinational corporations including staffing, training and development, performance management, expatriation and repatriation, and compensation.

title: Diversity Issues
description: Managing employees in a diverse workforce. Policy development for managing diversity. Legal issues in diversity.

title: Human Resource Analytics
description: Human Resource (HR) metrics and analytics. Introduction to the principles of applied research for evidence-based decision-making in organizations including data collection, research design, and statistical testing using actual data sets and analytics.

title: Venture Launch
description: Engage in real world entrepreneurial activities. Start a venture or examine the business potential of technology developed by faculty and/or students at SDSU.
notes: MGT 470 is not a subsititute for

title: Leadership in Organizations
description: Leadership, communicating vision, initiating changes and innovation, and developing leadership competencies through self-assessment.

title: Lean Startup Applications to National Security Challenges
description: Applications of the Lean-Startup methodology to assessing problems posed by national security agencies such as the U.S. Department of Defense. To include problem / solution fit, market analysis, and business model development using the Mission Model Canvas framework.
notes: Prior military experience is a plus but not a requirement for participation in this course.

title: Selected Topics in Management
description: Selected areas of concern in management.
notes: Limit of nine units of any combination of 296, 496, 596 courses applicable to a bachelor’s degree. See

title: Investigation and Report
description: A comprehensive and original study of a problem connected with management under the direction of one or more members of the management staff.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Advanced Topics in Management
description: Advanced special topics in management.

title: Seminar in Selected Topics
description: Intensive study in specific areas of management.

title: Seminar in World Business Environment
description: Nature, dimensions and motives of international business. Impact of environmental factors. Nature of multinational corporation, importance of national and multilateral controls and policies for international business management.

title: Seminar in Group Processes and Leadership
description: Perceptions and processes in work groups. Experience in interpersonal networks, influence and rewards, stereotypes; managing differences and conflicts.

title: Seminar in Business Ethics and Social Institutions
description: Ethical and social aspects of current issues in business and society. Changing role of stakeholders including consumers, shareholders, and employees. Assessment of operation, functioning and regulation of the market system.

title: Entrepreneurship
description: Examination of the entrepreneurial approach; concepts, theory and techniques of managerial innovation and implementation; analysis of entrepreneurial skills.

title: Seminar in Organizational Issues
description: Issues in organizations in modern society: organization design, environmental interface, and political processes.

title: Seminar in Managing the Growing Firm
description: Problems and issues confronting entrepreneurs beyond start-up of a new venture. Focus on issues from both entrepreneur and investor perspectives.

title: Seminar in Corporate Governance
description: Roles and interrelationships among members of corporate governance triad: managers, directors, and shareholders. History and theories of corporate governance, ethical obligations underlying the three roles, and case studies.

title: Seminar in International Entrepreneurship and Business Development
description: Challenges and issues confronting entrepreneurs seeking to develop international business opportunities. Concepts, theory, and techniques of international entrepreneurship. Drivers of entrepreneurship and assessment of entrepreneurial conditions around the world.

title: Research
description: Research in the area of management.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.
